data.name: Ehsanun
data.gender_notes: Ehsanun is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Arabic word 'ehsan' meaning to be kind, to make something beautiful, to bestow grace and kindness upon someone. This name is deeply rooted in Islamic spirituality and conveys a sense of elegance, charm, and compassion. The name Ehsanun carries the meaning “Grace, beauty, kindness” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Ehsanun usually hope their child will grow to embody grace, beauty, kindness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes the grace and beauty of Allah, and the kindness and generosity of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It is a reminder to always strive to be kind and gracious in all aspects of life, and to bestow beauty and kindness upon others.
data.etymology: Ehsanun belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Grace, beauty, kindness.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ehsanun total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_english.name: Ehsanun
in_english.long_meaning: Ehsanun is a name that conveys goodness, beauty, and perfection. It is derived from the Arabic root 'hasana', which means 'to be good' or 'to be beautiful'. In Islamic tradition, Ehsanun is considered one of the beautiful names of Allah, and it is often used to describe someone who is kind, compassionate, and virtuous. The name Ehsanun is also associated with the concept of ihsan, which is the highest level of worship in Islam. It is the state of being in a constant state of devotion and obedience to Allah, and it is considered the ultimate goal of human existence. In modern times, the name Ehsanun is still used in many Muslim cultures, and it is often given to children born into families that value kindness, generosity, and compassion.
